Verenchanka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivetska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Verenchanka's Jewish community, present from the mid-16th century, numbered around 100 people in the early 20th century, its core made up of immigrants from Moldova and Galicia engaged mainly in agriculture, trade, and crafts; the Bnei Zion movement was established there in 1909, and Verenchanka's Jews took an active part in Bukovina's Jewish life through the 1930s. During the German-Romanian occupation, the community was deported to the Chernivtsi ghetto and the camps of Transnistria, sharing the fate of the region's other Jews.
